clue.text: Exercise before heading for something to drink

parts.note: PRE is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of 'something' is used

parts.note: first letter of something
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A workout routine followed by a reach for a refreshing beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise lifting the body by straightening the arms, called a push-up in the US.

clue.text: Veg and fruit, chopped

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter of the fruit is lost

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to cut up vegetables and fruit together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a green vegetable, and veg is the everyday short form of vegetable.

clue.text: Some fear a chest infection?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Worry that one might be catching a chest infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is often caused by an ear infection, so the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Cake is solid on top once cooked

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top means this letter is placed above the rest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for solid, as in chemistry's state symbols

indicators.note: cooked suggests something worked over and altered, so the letters of 'once' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baking tip: the cake has set firm on top once it has been in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small plain British baked item, a kind of cake often served with jam and cream.

clue.text: Course requiring permit to be getting on

parts.note: a pass is a permit allowing entry
to age is to grow older, to be getting on in years

explanation.surface: A training course that needs a permit before anyone can start.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a course or route through something, such as a passage of time or a passage through rocks.

clue.text: Primate guarding small part of church

indicators.note: guarding means standing around something, so the small letter goes inside the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A monkey or archbishop standing guard over a little corner of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Excellent oil beaten to make mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are whisked, so the letters of 'oil' are mixed up

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: whisk good oil to produce mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning excellent, gives AI because the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic-flavoured mayonnaise from Provence.

clue.text: Friends put up with criticism for comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'

explanation.surface: Pals tolerating harsh reviews of a comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical humour, a broad style of comedy with pratfalls.

clue.text: Botched raid when entering house in style

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the rearranged letters go inside the house abbreviation
botched means bungled, so the letters of 'raid' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A police raid goes wrong as they burst into a stylish house.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a hairstyle, the way someone's hair is arranged.

clue.text: Persevere with a new motto

parts.note: to slog is to keep working hard and persevere

explanation.surface: Advice to keep going with a fresh guiding principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase, a motto used by a campaign or brand.

clue.text: Career sites designed for office workers

indicators.note: designed means made up or put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Job-hunting websites built for people who work in offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretaries are administrative staff who handle correspondence and records in an office.

clue.text: Abrasive material also seen in Society publication

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so the word for also goes within the other pieces

parts.note: a paper is a newspaper, a publication
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A rough fabric spotted in a high-society magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is paper coated with grit, used as an abrasive for smoothing wood.

clue.text: Ruffles feathers in Scottish team, dismissing leader

indicators.note: dismissing the leader means the first letter of the team name is dropped

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A Scottish football club causes a stir by sacking its captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is one of Glasgow's two big football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle feathers is an idiom for upsetting people, which is what something that angers them does.

clue.text: Cunning tips from several rowers

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so the first and last letters of 'several' are used

parts.note: first and last letters of several
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Crafty advice picked up from a number of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning or dexterous trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Signal over top mathematician

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the signal word is read backwards

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act
a lid is a top for a container

explanation.surface: A sign that an outstanding mathematician has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer whose Elements founded geometry.

clue.text: Actor flying over India and a country in Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the rearranged letters sit above the rest
flying suggests letters in motion, so the letters of 'Actor' are rearranged

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor jetting over India and on to a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan nation on the Adriatic coast of Europe.

clue.text: Nasty individual chore?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 'nasty ...' is an unpleasant person
second meaning: a chore is literally a ..., a task, and the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is usually 'a nasty piece of work'; read literally it is just a task.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a disagreeable, spiteful person, while the literal words describe a single job to be done.

clue.text: Every other piece of jelly in the cream

indicators.note: every other piece means taking alternate letters, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A trifle recipe with alternating layers of jelly set into the cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the elite, as in 'the cream of society'.

clue.text: Etiquette surrounding university discussion group

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around, so the etiquette word holds the university letter

parts.note: form means proper conduct or etiquette, as in 'bad form'

explanation.surface: Rules of good manners at a university debating society.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or assembly where ideas are discussed.

clue.text: Season well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the season between winter and summer
second meaning: a source of water rising from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an adverb here but is the noun, a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the time of year after winter and a natural flow of water from underground.

clue.text: An allowance no single sailor rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
tar is an old term for a sailor

explanation.surface: A lone seaman turned down the offer of an allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies given to each person.

clue.text: Charm shown during job interview

indicators.note: shown during means visible within these words, the answer sitting across them

explanation.surface: Charisma displayed while being interviewed for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' suggests charisma, but here it is an amulet.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also spelt obeah, is a West Indian form of sorcery or a fetish used as a magic charm.

clue.text: Complimentary cover ultimately incorporated into cost

indicators.note: incorporated into means taken inside, so the letter goes within the cost

parts.note: a fee is a cost or charge

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of 'cover' is used

parts.note: last letter of cover

explanation.surface: Insurance cover that is thrown in at no extra charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Complimentary means given without charge, as with complimentary tickets.

clue.text: Section of orchestra in main pit, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Part of the band playing down in the orchestra pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, forming a percussion section of an orchestra.
